speaker: Doctor
text: Can you point to the exact location of your pain, and does it radiate up your forearm or into your fingers? I also need to know if you have experienced any recent trauma or repetitive strain to your wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the radiation of pain to your elbow and history of trauma, has your grip strength weakened significantly, and do you experience numbness or tingling in your thumb, index, or middle fingers?

REQUEST TEST: Nerve conduction study of the right upper extremity.

REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray right wrist and elbow.
